questions.q: What happens immediately after CREATE ROLE DRIFTWOOD_SUPPORT_ANALYST runs, before any GRANT statements?
options: The role can immediately query every table in the account
The role exists but has no privileges at all — it's an empty container until explicitly granted access
The role is automatically granted SELECT on every view in the current schema
The role automatically inherits all privileges of the user who created it
questions.explain: CREATE ROLE only defines the role's name — it starts with zero privileges until GRANT statements add them.

questions.q: Why are GRANT USAGE statements needed on the warehouse, database, and schema, in addition to any object-level grant?
options: Only the warehouse needs a USAGE grant; database and schema are automatic
USAGE grants replace the need for any SELECT grant entirely
USAGE grants are optional and only improve query performance
A role needs permission at every level between logging in and reading an object's data — missing any one link breaks the chain
questions.explain: Without USAGE at every level — warehouse, database, schema — a role can't reach an object even if it later gets SELECT on that object.

questions.q: Why does this lesson grant warehouse/database/schema USAGE now but defer the view's SELECT grant to Lesson 7?
options: The summary view doesn't exist until Lesson 7 creates it, so the object-level grant has to wait until the object exists
Snowflake requires a 24-hour delay between creating a role and granting SELECT
SELECT grants must always be issued before USAGE grants
The VP of Support has to approve the SELECT grant separately
questions.explain: You can't grant SELECT on an object that doesn't exist yet — the infrastructure-level USAGE grants are set up now, and the view-specific grant happens right after the view is created.

questions.q: Why does DRIFTWOOD_SUPPORT_ANALYST never get SELECT on RAW_TICKETS directly?
options: The role only needs to read the summarized view, not raw ticket rows, and least privilege means granting only what's actually needed
Snowflake does not allow SELECT grants on raw tables
Granting SELECT on a raw table is more expensive than granting it on a view
RAW_TICKETS is automatically dropped after the view is created
questions.explain: Least privilege means granting exactly the access a role needs to do its job — this role's job is reading the summary, not the raw rows.

questions.q: Why not just have the Support analyst use the admin role that's been used to build everything so far?
options: Snowflake limits each account to a single role
It would work today, but it would give the analyst far more access than their job needs, increasing the blast radius of any mistake or compromised password
Admin roles cannot run SELECT statements
Admin roles are automatically disabled after a project is built
questions.explain: Using a narrowly scoped role keeps the damage from a mistake or a compromised credential limited to what that role can actually touch.
